title: Scheme base changes of a sheaf coproduct of open subfunctors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work on its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $X$ over $S$ write $h_X(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,X)$. Let $F$ and $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ be sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], indexed by a small set $I$, with subfunctor inclusions $\iota_i:F_i\hookrightarrow F$ [def-pc-subfunctor] representable by open immersions [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $H=\coprod_{i\in I}F_i$ be their coproduct in sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with injections $j_i$, and let $q:H\to F$ satisfy $qj_i=\iota_i$. For every scheme $T$ over $S$ and map $t:h_T\to F$, let $V_i\hookrightarrow T$ represent $h_T\times_FF_i$, and form the scheme coproduct $C_T=\coprod_iV_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], assumed to lie in the chosen big site. The functors $h_X$ are fppf sheaves. The maps $h_{V_i}\to H\times_Fh_T$ induce a canonical isomorphism of fppf sheaves $h_{C_T}\simeq H\times_Fh_T$ over $h_T$, whose restriction to every summand is the specified map and which commutes with every change of scheme test $T'\to T$. In particular $q$ is representable and its scheme base change along $t$ is the morphism $C_T\to T$ induced by the inclusions $V_i\hookrightarrow T$. No covering condition on the $V_i$ and no algebraic-space condition on $F_i$ or $H$ is assumed.

proof.text: Every fppf covering is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to a compatible family of maps into any scheme $X$. This gives a unique underlying scheme map. When all local maps are over $S$, its composite into $S$ agrees locally with the structure map, so uniqueness in the same descent lemma with target $S$ makes it an $S$-map. Thus every $h_X$ satisfies the fppf sheaf equalizer condition. Products with an equality condition satisfy the same condition componentwise; in particular $P_T(W)=\{(a,b):a\in H(W),\ b:W\to T,\ q(a)=t(b)\}$ is the sheaf $H\times_Fh_T$.

Write $k_i:V_i\to C_T$ and $v_i:V_i\to T$, and let $s_i\in F_i(V_i)$ be the universal section of the specified representing isomorphism. The coproduct property of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] gives $p:C_T\to T$ with $pk_i=v_i$. Its summands are a clopen partition. The converse gluing in [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] gives $a_C\in H(C_T)$ restricting to $j_i(s_i)$. The maps $k_i$ form an fppf cover by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]; hence $q(a_C)=t(p)$, since both restrict to $\iota_i(s_i)=t(v_i)$. Define $\Phi_W(g)=(g^*a_C,pg)$ for $g:W\to C_T$. This is natural in $W$ and its summand restrictions are the required maps. For the universe sizes in Lean, first discard empty summands. Choosing a point in each remaining summand injects its index set into the points of C_T: distinct indices are separated using the map from the coproduct to the binary coproduct of terminal schemes that labels one summand by the first injection and all others by the second. Thus the support is small in the scheme universe. Reindex it by a small type, compare the given cofan with the canonical scheme coproduct, and transport openness, disjointness and joint surjectivity. Sheaf descent on this cover also proves that the lifted representables of the summands form a coproduct in sheaves.

proof.text: For $(a,b)\in P_T(W)$, [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] gives the unique decomposition $W=\coprod_iW_i$ and $a_i\in F_i(W_i)$ with $j_i(a_i)=a|_{W_i}$. The equation defining $P_T(W)$ restricts to $\iota_i(a_i)=t(b|_{W_i})$. By the given representing property of $V_i$ there is a unique $g_i:W_i\to V_i$ with projections $(a_i,b|_{W_i})$. The scheme coproduct decomposition of $W$ gives a unique $g:W\to C_T$ restricting to $k_ig_i$. Define $\Psi_W(a,b)=g$. This uses no covering property of the opens $V_i\subset T$.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first paragraph, coproduct base-change comparison; detailed sectionwise verification using Tags 0F15 and 02WO.

proof.text: The construction in Step 2, together with the cartesian clause of [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition], makes each square from h_{V_i} to h_{C_T} over F_i to H cartesian. The map g of Step 3 has the prescribed two projections, as is checked on the partition pieces, which form an fppf cover by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. For another map with these projections, the first family of cartesian squares factors its restrictions through V_i; the given representing square for V_i then identifies each such factor with g_i. The scheme coproduct property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] gives equality globally. Thus every compatible pair has exactly one lift, including empty pieces, and the comparison square is cartesian. This argument uses the definition of open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] to identify the open summands and their monomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first paragraph, coproduct base-change comparison; detailed sectionwise verification using Tags 0F15 and 02WO.

proof.text: Express the preceding unique lifting property on each test W as the pullback criterion in sets. Limits of presheaves are computed objectwise, so the already natural morphisms a_C and h_p form a cartesian presheaf square. Its canonical isomorphism with the categorical pullback is the desired comparison, and Step 1 identifies these presheaves with sheaves. Its summand equations characterize its first projection by the sheaf coproduct of representables proved in Step 2; its second projection is h_p. Pullback extensionality therefore gives uniqueness of the isomorphism. This implements the sectionwise inverse of [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] without a separate choice of an inverse natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first paragraph, coproduct base-change comparison; detailed sectionwise verification using Tags 0F15 and 02WO.

proof.text: For $f:T\prime\to T$, use $t\prime=t\circ h_f$ and the chosen representing opens $V_i\prime$. On $V_i\prime$ the universal pair gives a unique map $d_i:V_i\prime\to V_i$ over $f$, and the scheme coproduct property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] gives $d:C_{T\prime}\to C_T$. For a test $W$, the two comparison maps send $g:W\to C_{T\prime}$ to the same pair $(g^*a_{C_{T\prime}},f p\prime g)$: this holds on each inverse-image summand by the definition of $d_i$, and holds globally by the sheaf condition of Step 1. Thus the isomorphisms commute with $f$. The sectionwise description also identifies $h_{C_{T\prime}}$ with $h_{C_T}\times_{h_T}h_{T\prime}$: a pair $(g,b\prime)$ with $pg=f b\prime$ corresponds under $\Phi$ to $(g^*a_C,b\prime)$ and then under $\Psi$ for $T\prime$ to its unique map into $C_{T\prime}$. This verifies the full base-change assertion. In Lean the last assertion follows by pullback pasting for the two comparison squares, reflection along the fully faithful lifted Yoneda functor, and preservation of pullbacks by the forgetful functor from schemes over S. The uniqueness of each d_i follows from the open-immersion monomorphism V_i to T [def-weil-open-immersion], and uniqueness of d follows from the scheme cofan.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first paragraph, coproduct base-change comparison; detailed sectionwise verification using Tags 0F15 and 02WO.

proof.text: For every $T,t$, Steps 2-5 exhibit $h_{C_T}\simeq H\times_Fh_T$, and its projection is $p$, restricting to $v_i$ on each summand. This is exactly representability of $q$ in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Step 6 gives the stated test-change compatibility. For $I=\varnothing$, the partition theorem says $H(W)$ is empty for nonempty $W$ and a singleton for empty $W$, agreeing with $h_{\varnothing}(W)$; empty summands cause the same unique empty-piece maps throughout.

lean.statement: theorem openSheafCoproduct_baseChange {S : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type (max u v)} (F : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (Fi : I → Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (ι : ∀ i, Fi i ⟶ F) (hmono : ∀ i, Mono (ι i)) (hopen : ∀ i, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWithLift (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (ι i).hom) (H : Sheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (Type (max u v))) (j : ∀ i, Fi i ⟶ H) (hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j)) (q : H ⟶ F) (hfac : ∀ i, j i ≫ q = ι i) (hsite : ∀ (T : Over S) (t : uliftYoneda.{v}.obj T ⟶ F.obj), Nonempty (OpenSheafCoproductTest Fi ι T t)) : (∀ X : Over S, Presheaf.IsSheaf (fppfTopology.over S) (uliftYoneda.{v}.obj X)) ∧ AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableLift q.hom ∧ ∀ (T : Over S) (t : uliftYoneda.{v}.obj T ⟶ F.obj) (D : OpenSheafCoproductTest Fi ι T t), ∃! e : uliftYoneda.{v}.obj D.C ≅ pullback q.hom t, D.ComparisonEquations j q e ∧ ∀ (T' : Over S) (f : T' ⟶ T) (D' : OpenSheafCoproductTest Fi ι T' (uliftYoneda.{v}.map f ≫ t)), ∃! d : D'.C ⟶ D.C, (∀ i, ∃! di : D'.V i ⟶ D.V i, uliftYoneda.{v}.map di ≫ D.sectionMap i = D'.sectionMap i ∧ di ≫ D.inclusion i = D'.inclusion i ≫ f ∧ D'.injection i ≫ d = di ≫ D.injection i) ∧ d ≫ D.p = D'.p ≫ f ∧ IsPullback d.left D'.p.left D.p.left f.left ∧ ∀ e' : uliftYoneda.{v}.obj D'.C ≅ pullback q.hom (uliftYoneda.{v}.map f ≫ t), D'.ComparisonEquations j q e' → (uliftYoneda.{v}.map d ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.fst q.hom t = e'.hom ≫ pullback.fst q.hom (uliftYoneda.{v}.map f ≫ t)) ∧ (uliftYoneda.{v}.map d ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd q.hom t = e'.hom ≫ pullback.snd q.hom (uliftYoneda.{v}.map f ≫ t) ≫ uliftYoneda.{v}.map f)
